rule: Use the AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS sentinel from version_compat instead of inline packaging.version.parse comparisons for Airflow version guards
trigger: packaging.version.parse(airflow_version) compared against a literal version string inside a provider
rationale: The repo provides pre-computed version sentinels (e.g. AIRFLOW_V_3_1_PLUS) in airflow.providers.fab.version_compat; using raw packaging.version.parse is verbose and inconsistent with the canonical pattern

rule: Do not mutate Flask-AppBuilder's global Model.metadata at import time; scope metadata overrides to Airflow's own mapper registry only
trigger: Model.metadata = ... or assignment to Base.metadata at module level inside the FAB provider
rationale: Mutating FAB's shared Model.metadata at import time silently overrides naming conventions and schema config for all code importing FAB's Model, not just Airflow's own tables

evidence.excerpt: global side effect changes Model.metadata for all code importing Flask-AppBuilder

rule: Prefer removing existing type: ignore suppressions rather than adding new suppression codes
trigger: diff adds a new mypy error code to an existing # type: ignore comment
rationale: Airflow reviewers explicitly ask contributors to look for ways to remove existing ignores instead of broadening suppression lists

evidence.excerpt: we should be looking for ways to remove existing ignores instead of adding more

rule: When running under Uvicorn (ASGI), remove the Flask/Werkzeug Date response header unconditionally so the server emits only one Date header
trigger: flask_app.after_request hook reads or conditionally removes the Date header when integrating with Uvicorn
rationale: Flask's Date header is added before Uvicorn adds its own; conditional removal still results in duplicate headers because Flask's header is not visible to Uvicorn's layer

evidence.excerpt: remove the Date header from Flask response unconditionally so only server-provided Date is emitted

rule: Derive the secure-cookie flag from both the request scheme and the ssl_cert config, not from ssl_cert alone
trigger: secure = bool(conf.get('api', 'ssl_cert', fallback='')) without checking request.base_url.scheme
rationale: SSL termination may happen upstream; relying solely on ssl_cert misses HTTPS requests that arrive without a configured cert path

rule: Use spec= or autospec= when creating Mock objects for SQLAlchemy sessions and ORM model instances in Airflow tests
trigger: Mock() or MagicMock() without spec= used for a session, role, or permission object in a provider test
rationale: Unspecced mocks allow tests to pass with invalid attribute/method usage; Airflow testing expectations require spec'd mocks for session and ORM objects

evidence.excerpt: Using spec/autospec aligns better with Airflow's testing expectations

rule: When a provider imports an API added in a recent version of another provider, guard the import with a try/except ImportError and early-return to maintain compatibility with older provider versions
trigger: unconditional import of a symbol from another provider's recently-added API module (e.g. airflow.providers.openlineage.api.*)
rationale: Providers have independent release cycles; an unconditional import of a newly added API breaks installations running an older version of the dependency provider

evidence.excerpt: will not work with older OL provider; api was added recently, so we need try/except and early return

rule: In Google provider hooks, decompose compound resource-name strings (e.g. projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{id}) into individual parameters rather than accepting the full name as a single argument
trigger: a Google provider hook method accepts a parameter named `name` typed as str that represents a full GCP resource path
rationale: The common practice in the google provider is to split compound resource names into constituent parts (project_id, location, resource_id) as seen in endpoint_service.py and other hooks

evidence.excerpt: common practice in google provider is to divide the name by parts

rule: Hook method parameter types must match the corresponding Google Cloud client library types exactly, not be widened to Any
trigger: a Google provider hook method uses Any for a parameter whose client counterpart has a concrete type (e.g. types.DeleteAgentEngineConfigOrDict)
rationale: Using Any instead of the client library type loses static checking and diverges from the client contract; reviewers require parity with the client's declared types

evidence.excerpt: type should be consistent with type in the Client; client uses types.DeleteAgentEngineConfigOrDict

rule: In Google provider hooks that use @GoogleBaseHook.fallback_to_default_project_id, describe project_id as optional in the docstring and position it last in the parameter list
trigger: a hook method decorated with @GoogleBaseHook.fallback_to_default_project_id documents project_id as 'Required' or places it before other parameters
rationale: The fallback decorator supplies a default project_id, making it optional; describing it as required and placing it early in the signature is misleading and inconsistent with other Google provider hooks

evidence.excerpt: project_id described as required when default implies optional; should be moved to end

rule: Operator execute_complete methods must branch explicitly on success, timeout, and error trigger statuses rather than collapsing all non-success states into a single error branch
trigger: execute_complete contains if event['status'] != 'success': raise ... without separate handling for timeout
rationale: Timeout and error are distinct outcomes; collapsing them loses actionable information and prevents callers from distinguishing transient failures from hard errors

evidence.excerpt: explicitly branch on success, timeout and error

rule: Every Google provider operator execute method must emit a self.log.info call describing the operation being performed
trigger: an operator execute() method in providers/google that calls a hook without a preceding or following self.log.info()
rationale: Consistent with the established pattern in google provider operators (e.g. endpoint_service.py); reviewers explicitly require log.info for observability

evidence.excerpt: could you add a self.log.info for this method as in endpoint_service.py

rule: Connection environment variable examples in provider docs must use URI format (not JSON object format) for AIRFLOW_CONN_* variables
trigger: provider .rst doc contains export AIRFLOW_CONN_<ID>='{...}' with a JSON object literal
rationale: Airflow's env-var connection backend parses AIRFLOW_CONN_* as URIs, not JSON; JSON examples are rejected or silently misparsed

evidence.excerpt: AIRFLOW_CONN_ env variable is parsed as URI, not JSON; this example will be rejected

rule: Provider pyproject.toml workaround dependencies must include a comment explaining the upstream issue and when the workaround can be removed
trigger: a transitive or pinned dependency added to pyproject.toml with only a brief inline comment but no upstream issue reference or removal condition
rationale: Reviewers require workaround pins to document the upstream library that needs fixing, a link to an open issue, and the condition under which the pin can be dropped

evidence.excerpt: add instructions on when/how we will remove it and link upstream issue

rule: When a new operator parameter will have its default value changed in a future release, accept None as the unset sentinel, default to None, and raise FutureWarning when None is detected rather than using the final default directly
trigger: a new operator __init__ parameter is added with a default value that a reviewer notes will change in a future release
rationale: Airflow must warn users before changing defaults to avoid silent breaking changes; the None-sentinel + FutureWarning pattern allows the current behaviour while signalling the upcoming change

evidence.excerpt: accept None as unset, set to True + raise FutureWarning about expected change

rule: URL substring checks used for security-sensitive routing must validate that the trusted substring appears at the expected position (e.g. as the hostname), not anywhere in the URL string
trigger: if '<trusted-domain>' in url or similar substring check used to authenticate or route a request
rationale: An attacker can craft a URL that contains the trusted substring at an arbitrary position (e.g. as a path component), bypassing the check; positional validation is required

evidence.excerpt: trusted substring may be at an arbitrary position in the sanitized URL
